title: Chapter 77: The Paper and Pen on the Table
html:
The taxi driver’s strange behavior unsettled Chen Ge. No one knew a city’s streets better than its cabbies, including the places people knew to avoid.

Has the driver misunderstood me?

The mat lay in the mud, quickly soaking through in the rain. The supernatural stories about Mu Yang High School had not seemed all that frightening when Chen Ge read them. After the encounter with the taxi driver, however, his confidence began to waver.

The mission only requires me to survive. Even the black phone thinks that will be a serious challenge.

In moments, the taxi vanished down the road. Chen Ge stood alone in his raincoat, surrounded by an endless expanse of trees. He might as well have been abandoned in the wilderness.

The rain kept pouring. Chen Ge drew his raincoat tighter, took out his flashlight, and followed the muddy road. Low clouds blotted out the moon. Only as he approached the buildings did their true state of decay become clear.

Rusted chains hung from the doors, and the windows had long since lost their glass. Through the gaps, Chen Ge saw rooms crammed with rotting furniture and garbage while unfamiliar insects crawled across the floor.

Not a single sign of life. Is this place really that cursed?

Before coming, Chen Ge had gleaned a few useful details from Fan Yu’s aunt, so he knew something about the area around Mu Yang High School. With no one to ask for directions, he could only press deeper into the darkness and trust his memory.

Rain had turned the road to mud. Gnarled, untrimmed trees crowded in from both sides, their branches encroaching on the path.

Mu Yang High School was built on the site of a crematorium. As frightening as that sounds, there must have been a road wide enough for vehicles. But this path keeps narrowing. No car could make it through here. Am I even going the right way?The heavy rain slowed his progress. Getting lost out here would be bad. If Mu Yang High School isn’t at the end of this road, I’ll have to turn back and abandon the mission.

Chen Ge followed the road for another thirty minutes. At its end, he found a fallen sign and a wooden fence.

Lichen has grown along one side. It must have been lying here for years.

Chen Ge pulled the sign upright, but its characters were too faded to read. He swept his flashlight across it. Why is there lichen on only one side? Is it because of the sun, or did someone recently move the sign and fence?

He stopped and checked the time on his phone. It’s almost eight, and I still haven’t found the mission location. At least I have a signal. If something goes wrong, I can call for help.

The rain made the night unnaturally dark. For miles around, Chen Ge’s phone was the only visible light. The sign and fence are both here, but they look as if they were moved recently. Strange.

Chen Ge used the sign to push aside the shrubs blocking his path. Ten meters farther on, the landscape changed. A line of broken wooden railings stood amid the trees, enclosing several squat buildings.

This is Mu Yang High School?

The school was far more dilapidated than Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy and less than a third its size.

Its smaller size did not put Chen Ge at ease. There was less ground to explore, but also fewer places to hide.

Chen Ge tossed the sign aside and vaulted the railing into Mu Yang High School. From there, he could take in the entire campus at a glance.

The education block stood closest to the entrance. A massive fire had charred its exterior black, and cracks ran through the corners as though the walls might collapse at any moment.

The two-story dormitory stood to the left, its handful of rooms reflecting the school’s tiny enrollment. To the right, the office building appeared to be the best preserved.

Behind the education block was an uneven field. Two basketball courts and several ping pong tables stood to the side.

That was the entirety of Mu Yang High School. Beyond its wealth of supernatural stories, the campus itself had little character. Chen Ge suspected the true reason for its closure was not paranormal at all; perhaps no new students had wanted to study there.

Oddly, reaching his destination calmed Chen Ge. He had always been good at controlling his emotions.

There are four side missions at Mu Yang High School: The Pen Spirit, The Fifth Cubicle in the Toilet, Deep Well, and The Sealed Classroom. If I want to unlock the full scenario, I mustn’t miss out on any of them.

In the previous mission, a completion rate above ninety percent had earned him the hidden reward—Wang Qi’s Missing Person Notice. That item had forged a connection between him and Xiaoxiao’s family.

He understood the importance of having a high mission completion rate, but it was easier said than done. Any one of the side missions could rival the creepiness of a Nightmare Mission, and he was expected to complete all four in one night.

It isn’t midnight yet. The residents of the other world won’t be active for a while. I should scout all four locations. If they look too dangerous, I’ll still have time to leave.

Chen Ge tucked the doll against his chest, drew his trusty mallet, and headed for the education block.

Even after so many years, soot still blackened the building’s exterior.

The whole building burned. Could that be connected to the old crematorium?

Chen Ge moved quietly, recalling the mission description on the black phone.

“There’s a classroom at the end of the corridor that’s always sealed. No one ever enters it, but every night, the classroom will come alive with activity.”

Fan Yu’s father met with disaster after entering that classroom. It may be the center of Mu Yang High School’s paranormal activity.

The eerie photograph surfaced in his mind. There was a good chance he would spend the night with a classroom full of students who had refused to face the camera.

Every classroom was locked, leaving Chen Ge to peer through the windows by flashlight. The first few were ordinary abandoned rooms. Only when he reached the final classroom at the end of the corridor did he notice something strange.

The fire had inexplicably spared the classroom. What drew Chen Ge’s attention, however, were the books, paper, and pen arranged on a table in the center, as though someone had just finished a lesson.
